about: The Watching strip above a session's composer: the sentence an opened strip says about each
watch, the line it adds when nobody is checking one, the sentence its folded line writes over
several targets, and a session target's word — one set of cases both clients are proved
against. The web reads this file in `lib/watches.test.ts` (`stripSentence`, `stripStaleLine`,
`stripCounts`, `SESSION_TARGET_WORDS`), the native client in `WatchStripCopyParityTests`
(`WatchProjection.stripSentence`, `stripStaleLine`, `WatchSessionSummary.lineCounts`,
`SessionStatusGlyph.make(runState:)`), so the two ends cannot drift into two sentences.
Every time here is read against `now`.
`sentences`: one watch → its sentence. `targets` are the watch's targets by kind, a
`:GONE` suffix marking one whose row was deleted (it is not counted). The condition is said of
the live targets — `it` for one, `all of them` / `any of them` for several — and the deadline
is the time left until `expiresAt`, in the strip's spans.
`stale`: one watch → the line an opened strip adds under its sentence, or null. Only an ACTIVE
watch nobody has looked at for more than three minutes (since `lastEvaluatedAt`, or since
`createdAt` when it was never looked at) says one.
`counts`: the distinct live targets of the strip's watches, each with its `targetStatus` (null
when the account cannot read the row) → the folded line's sentence, which is Tasks created
here's (`session-created-tasks.fixture.json`). A task is done when its status is DONE; a
session when it is neither running, queued nor failed — its turn is over.
`sessionWords`: a session target's run state → the word its pill says, the one its own
header's glyph says for that run state.
`rows`: the live RESUME_SESSION watches one session is the observer of → what its session list
row says about the wait: `word`, the header's word, which the row's glyph says as its tooltip,
and `line`, the row's second line — the strip's folded line in one string. One live target left
is named, however many watches wait on it: `Watching <title>`. Otherwise what the wait needs (a lone watch's
threshold, or the distinct live targets across several) and then the `counts` sentence over
them. With every watch paused it leads with the paused word instead of `Watching`. Targets carry
an `id`, so two watches naming one target count it once, and `state` GONE when deleted. The web
reads this in `lib/watches.test.ts` (`watchingSessions`), the native client in
`WatchStripCopyParityTests` (`WatchSessionSummary.rowLine` and `.word`).
`fold`: the live RESUME_SESSION watches one session is the observer of, as the watch read sends
them → how the cards above its composer and its watching words fold a task and its run session
into one target. A target's `task` is its `targetTask`, the task its session runs: absent from an
older server, null for a session that runs no task. A session target that carries one counts as a
target on that task — its id, its title, where it stands — and anything else stays as it is.
`watchedTasks`: what the Tasks card is given, one per live task target or run session, each
flagged stale when its watch has gone unchecked (two waits on one task are one row there).
`strip`: the watches, by index, the Watching strip keeps — those still waiting on something that
is not a task or its run — and none is no strip. `taskStaleLines`: the unchecked lines the opened
Tasks card puts at its top, for the watches the strip does not keep. `word` and `line` as in
`rows`. `card`, where given, names the `session-created-tasks.fixture.json` card case these
watched tasks are the `watched` of. The web reads this in `lib/watches.test.ts` (`watchedTasks`,
`waitsBeyondTasks`, `taskStaleLines`, `watchingSessions`), OrbitKit in `WatchStripCopyParityTests`
and Android in `WatchStripCopyParityTest` (`WatchSessionSummary`'s `watchedTasks`, `beyondTasks`,
`taskStaleLines`, `rowLine` and `word`).
